item.title: ‘I couldn’t disappear’ – Oliver Bearman rues “crazy” penalty for Pierre Gasly clash
item.description: Motorsport photo Oliver Bearman says he was “pretty shocked” to land a 10-second penalty for his collision with Pierre Gasly in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix. Bearman gained two spots on the opening lap of the Austin race and made a move on 10th-placed Gasly on the next tour, down the inside in Turn 13. Realising the gap was disappearing, Bearman put two wheels on the yellow inside kerb, but his front-left wheel still touched the Alpine ’s sidepod; the contact, albeit tenuous, caused significant damage to both cars, and FIA stewards hit the Briton with that 10-second penalty. “I was pretty shocked to be honest,” Bearman said. “If anything, it was a racing incident. I felt a bit hard done by for it to be a 10-second penalty as well, especially given some of the incidents that have happened this year that have gone either unpenalized or five-second penalty. Ten seconds for that type of incident seems very excessive in my opinion, given what happened. “I felt like I had enough of my car alongside to justify, or to kind of feel like I earned a bit of space, and didn't really get that space. I was given maybe half a car width. I was climbing up onto the kerb trying to avoid contact, but I simply couldn't. I couldn't disappear once I decided to go for the move. I didn't lock up, I didn't lose any control, it was just simply I couldn't disappear at that stage. Ten seconds is crazy, given all of those facts. Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team “To be honest, the more penalizing thing was that I picked up a bit of damage. It was a very small touch, but it loosened basically the floorboard and that slowly vibrated its way off over the next few laps, and the car was just deteriorating. I had maybe five laps where I was actually feeling very good and everything was fine and then slowly, step by step, the car was getting worse and then it was game over basically.” The damage led Bearman to let team-mate Esteban Ocon through on lap 11. “Pierre overtook me and I still felt relatively competitive,” the Haas driver continued. “The gap was very stable between Pierre in front and Esteban behind; it was just over one second. “But then from one lap to the next, we saw something fall off the car. And in sector one, I lost something like eight tenths to myself from one lap to the next. It was very clear that suddenly I went from having a bit of damage on the car to having a catastrophic amount of damage on the car. “I just said, ‘I'm not in this race anymore, I'm going to let Esteban go’. item.title: Andoni Iraola confirms double Liverpool injury blow ahead of Chelsea clash
item.description: Andoni Iraola confirms double Liverpool injury blow ahead of Chelsea clash Liverpool Fitness Update Ahead of Chelsea Carabao Cup Clash Liverpool go into Wednesday night’s Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against Chelsea with momentum, and with a few familiar selection headaches. Four straight wins have steadied the mood at Anfield, the latest a 2-0 victory over Brighton, and now Andoni Iraola must decide who is fit enough to keep that run going. The biggest immediate question surrounds Florian Wirtz. The early signs are positive. Iraola did not overplay it, but his message was clear enough. “We still have to wait. We train later. Florian [Wirtz] was quite fine and optimistic he would be available,” the Liverpool head coach said. That points to availability, barring any late setback. With Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz, the picture is far less encouraging. Iraola was cautious and, importantly, realistic. “And with Dom and Victor, I’m not so sure. I don’t want to say no, but I think it’s more difficult than Florian,” he added. That sounds like a manager preparing for the likelihood of being without both. Florian Wirtz Offers Timely Boost For Liverpool, Wirtz matters. In cup ties like this, control between the lines and quick decision-making can tilt the game. If he is fit enough to start, Iraola gets an obvious creative lift against a Chelsea side arriving with issues of their own. Photo: IMAGO Dominik Szoboszlai And Victor Munoz Doubts Remain Szoboszlai and Munoz look set to lose their race against time. Iraola has not ruled either player out completely, but the wording tells the story. Liverpool may have to manage without two useful options, one a midfield runner, the other a depth piece who can help rotation in a packed schedule. Chelsea Arrive With Problems Of Their Own Chelsea come to Anfield after a 2-0 defeat to Tottenham and without suspended Cole Palmer. Emiliano Martinez and Reece James are also absent. Xabi Alonso returns to Anfield as Chelsea head coach, but sentiment will not matter much here. Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 to reach this stage, Chelsea beat Leeds United 6-3, and this tie now looks shaped by availability as much as form. Right now, Liverpool have one likely boost in Wirtz, and two probable misses in Szoboszlai and Munoz. That is the short version, and it is probably the only one that matters before kick-off.

item.title: Xabi Alonso provides Joao Pedro injury update before Liverpool vs Chelsea
item.description: Xabi Alonso has confirmed that Chelsea forward Joao Pedro will be sidelined for “a few weeks” due to a thigh injury. The striker, who has scored five goals and made three assists in the Premier League this season, played no part in Chelsea’s bitter defeat against Tottenham on the weekend after missing out on the matchday squad due to injury. Alonso said the Brazilian felt something in training and had “a lot of fluid” in his thigh, with the club conducting further assessments to determine the extent of the blow. Chelsea felt Joao Pedro ’s absence up top in a toothless performance at home to Spurs and Alonso has now provided a further update on his status ahead of the club’s Carabao Cup fourth-round tie at Liverpool , revealing that Chelsea will have to adapt. "He has an injury on his thigh,” Joao Pedro confirmed. “He will be a few weeks out. Let's see how many. We don't want to predict on that. "He's a key player. We will miss him. But we have to be ready to deal with the injury and be competitive and win games with the players we have available. This is the situation." Joao Pedro suffered a knee injury which ruled him out of Chelsea’s match with Brentford ahead of the September international break, and he withdrew from Brazil duty. He returned to the Chelsea team to score twice against Bournemouth and then played 90 minutes against Everton at the beginning of October, but was absent for the Spurs loss. Morgan Rogers led the line on the weekend but had little impact, meaning Alonso could opt to start 35-year-old summer recruit Danny Welbeck, who has started both previous Carabao Cup ties this season. Estevao, meanwhile, could be in store for more minutes as Chelsea look to cope without Cole Palmer following his red card. “They are in the squad so every player in the squad can play,” Alonso added.

item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE, IN - OCTOBER 10: Purdue Boilermakers running back Fame Ijeboi (2) runs with the ball during the college football game between the Purdue Boilermakers and Minnesota Golden Gophers on October 10, 2026, at Ross-Ade Stadium in West Lafayette, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When Notre Dame quarterback C.J. Carr’s pass fell incomplete in the end zone as the game clock expired ( or did it? ), the celebration was on at LaVell Edwards Stadium. In a battle of two undefeated Top 10 teams, BYU had emerged the victor, upsetting the Fighting Irish and taking their spot as the No. 2-ranked team in the country. The Cougars were at the top of mountain. A week later, they came tumbling down. UCF was 3-3 and coming off back-to-back double-digit road losses to Houston and Oklahoma State. The Scott Frost-coached Knights returned home to face BYU in a back-and-forth contest that saw six lead changes in regulation before the two teams went to overtime deadlocked at 24-24. UCF won 39-31 when the Cougars failed to score in double-overtime. How could the same BYU team that beat Notre Dame lose to UCF a week later? Welcome to college football in 2026. BYU was not the only team knocked from the undefeated ranks this past weekend. No. 8-ranked Texas Tech trailed 24-6 at halftime to unranked Cincinnati and ended up losing 37-24 despite a second half rally. And No. 11-ranked Tennessee lost on a last-second field goal to a South Carolina squad with a 3-3 record. The previous week, the top-ranked Georgia Bulldogs were handed their first defeat of the season by an Auburn team with a 3-2 record. The Tigers then lost by three scores to No. 18-ranked LSU this past weekend. This is what parity looks like. Every college football fans wants it — until it comes for their team. It’s how the Minnesota Golden Gophers can beat three ranked teams in the span of five weeks and somehow sandwich an inexplicable blowout loss to 2-3 Purdue team in the middle. There are Gopher fans who will chalk this up to business as usual under head coach P.J. Fleck. They’re not necessarily wrong. Minnesota fans are no stranger to the inexplicable loss. There were the losses to Bowling Green (4-8) and Illinois (5-7) in 2021, and the losses to Illinois (5-7) and Purdue (4-8) in 2023. item.title: ESPN reveals surprising factor that prompted Man Utd board’s shocking Carrick U-turn
item.description: ESPN reveals surprising factor that prompted Man Utd board’s shocking Carrick U-turn The Manchester United hierarchy decided to give Michael Carrick a new lifeline despite the abysmal results and performances. The fallen Premier League giants are currently lying in a shocking 16th place in the standings, having collected a single win in eight league fixtures. They are also without a victory in their last eight matches across all competitions. The humbling back-to-back defeats to Como (1-4) and Bournemouth (0-3) were initially perceived as the end of the line for Carrick, who also had a row with Bruno Fernandes due to the captain’s public criticism. But against all odds, Carrick somehow survived the storm. Several sources, including The Athletic journalist Laurie Whitwell, revealed that the 45-year-old will remain in charge until the Chelsea game on Saturday. Why INEOS decided to keep Michael Carrick at the helm (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) Carrick’s confirmation has also been reported by ESPN journalists Rob Dawson and Mark Ogden. Interestingly, the source added that the hierarchy’s decision was influenced by the Old Trafford faithful, who made their feelings abundantly clear during and after Sunday’s defeat to Bournemouth. Despite the woeful showing, the fans expressed their overwhelming support for Carrick , who was visibly moved as he gratefully saluted all corners of the stadium while making his way to the tunnel. Once the manager was out of sight, the cheers immediately turned to jeers and whistles directed at the players, who have been accused of complacency. The club’s directors and owners were also targeted with insults throughout the game. PR management from Man Utd? (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) Carrick might be a popular figure at Old Trafford, but this doesn’t necessarily mean he’s the right man to take charge of the team for the rest of the season, especially amid the surfacing rifts between him and some of the senior players. As Jamie Carragher pointed out on Sunday, Carrick may not be the main culprit behind United’s ongoing woes, but his sacking could be a relief rather than a punishment, as he might not fancy coaching Fernandes and the rest of the group any longer. Therefore, the hierarchy’s decision to keep the Wallsend native could stem from a desire to avoid further fan backlash by sacking the most popular figure at the club rather than doing what’s best for the club. item.title: French Soccer Star Mbappé Apologizes For Mao Zedong Comment After Losing Chinese Sponsorships
item.description: Topline Kylian Mbappé apologized on Tuesday for comments he made referring to Mao Zedong as “a Chinese dictator”—remarks that prompted multiple sponsors in China to drop their deals with the French soccer star. Real Madrid's French forward Kylian Mbappe celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Spanish league football match between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid CF. AFP via Getty Images Key Facts Multiple Chinese companies, including beverage company Dongpeng and dairy producer Mengniu cut ties with Mbappé on Tuesday, with the beverage giant insisting it opposed “any conduct that hurts national sentiment.” The controversy stems from a clip shared by the French soccer podcast “The Bridge” where Mbappé describes what he thinks is the funniest internet meme of himself, where his face is photoshopped onto “some guy -- I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. While Mbappe doesn’t explicitly mention Mao by name, the video cut to a clip of his face being superimposed on an image of the former Chinese leader. The video prompted backlash on Chinese social media, and Bridge appears to have removed the clip from its social handles, but copies continue to be shared on Reddit and YouTube. Mbappé apologized for the comment later on Tuesday, calling it “ill-judged” and noting it “hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,” which he later insisted was “absolutely not my intention.” “I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry,” Mbappé wrote in a statement. Which Companies Dropped Mbappé? Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng (also known as Eastroc) and dairy company Mengniu both announced Tuesday that they were terminating their sponsorship agreements with Mbappé. In a statement shared with Beijing Daily, Dongpeng said it has a “zero-tolerance policy” towards any behavior that “offends national sentiments.” Mengniu, one of China’s biggest dairy companies, also issued a similar statement saying it “firmly opposes any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people.” Another Chinese company, cheese producer Milkground (also known as Miaokelanduo) also ended its partnership with Mbappé, the Associated Press reported. What Do We Know About Mbappé’s Annual Earnings? Mbappé, who ended as the top scorer of this year’s FIFA World Cup after taking his team to the semi-finals, ranked third on Forbes’ list of the Highest-Paid Soccer Players of 2026 . But this figure doesn’t include a key asset he added this year after ditching his long-time partnership with Nike and signing with Swiss-based athletic apparel brand On. item.title: Williams loses again - to opponent 28 years younger
item.description: Venus Williams has not won any of her 13 singles matches in 2026 [Getty Images] Former world number one Venus Williams lost for the 16th match in a row as she was beaten by an opponent 28 years younger. The 46-year-old American, who has won seven Grand Slam singles titles, was beaten 6-2 6-2 by 18-year-old Lilli Tagger at the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. It is the biggest age gap between opponents in a WTA match this decade and among the largest in tour-level history. Williams, ranked 599th in the world, has not won a match since July 2025 and relies on wildcards to play WTA tournaments. This latest defeat continues the debate over whether she deserves them. Some within the sport argue Williams is taking spots from younger players trying to develop their careers, but tournament organisers see the commercial value of inviting an all-time great. The Guangzhou fans clearly appreciated the chance to see the American superstar. A sizeable and enthusiastic crowd encouraged Williams and gave a huge ovation as she walked off court. Williams hasn't won for over a year - why does she get so many wildcards? Williams sisters exit US Open but excite - what does future hold? Williams won six of her Grand Slam singles titles - plus 30 WTA tournaments - before Austria's Tagger was born in February 2008. Tagger's coach Francesca Schiavone - the Italian former world number four who won the 2010 French Open - is the same age as Williams, and lost all eight meetings with the American during her playing career. "When I saw the draw I was super excited and a bit nervous - I respect her a lot," said Tagger, who is 53rd in the world. "It is funny she used to play with my coach. I would love to play at this age - I want to congratulate her." While the straight-set scoreline will embolden the critics, Williams did make Tagger - a rising talent who is predicted to have a bright future at the very top - work hard. However, the teenager proved far too good. The 2025 French Open girls' champion was superb on serve - dropping just seven service points and not facing a break point - while handling Williams' pace and crushing groundstrokes off both wings. Tagger broke her illustrious opponent's serve twice - for 1-0 and 5-2 leads - in two almost identical sets. At times, Williams was able to use her powerful serve to get out of trouble - fighting off 12 of 16 break points - and the veteran's trademark competitive spirit never wavered. item.title: Andoni Iraola Reflects on Squad Rotation and Chelsea Challenge
item.description: Coming out of the international break, Liverpool faced a gruelling stretch of four matches in just ten days. It’s a run that made the four day break between Villarreal last week in the Champions League and Brighton on Sunday in the Premier League feel practically luxurious. The norm this season for Liverpool and head coach Andoni Iraola, though, is going to be far more stretches with just two days between games than anything else—and that’s the situation they’re right back into as they prepare to face Chelsea in the League Cup on Wednesday. “It’s the same for everybody,” Iraola reflected at his pre-match press conference. “We don’t have time, Chelsea don’t have time, Arsenal doesn’t—so it can make a big difference if you have one more day. Against Brighton we were lucky because we had a few more days. “But everything has to be done on video when you don’t have time to prepare. Chelsea, Arsenal, Crystal Palace— definitely we will have less time to rest again but sometimes you have to adapt. You cannot overthink it or worry about it, it’s a matter of adapting to the situation.” Between Chelsea in the League Cup, Arsenal in the league, then Palace—with Fenerbahce in Europe between the Gunners and Eagles—it’s certainly going to be a busy stretch, but even Palace face a similar run with a League Cup tie and Hoffenheim in the Europa League. Iraola, though, has embraced of rotation in his early days as a Liverpool manager. In fact, it’s hard to recall any previous Liverpool manager being quite so willing to change up his starting eleven proactively, something that was a question mark at the start of the year. “All the top teams need to rotate,” Iraola added. “It’s not that we have more options, but sometimes you have rotation due to injury or sometimes different demands in games tactically. But I’m happy when we’ve had to use someone who hasn’t played a lot they’ve helped. “The more players in form the easier my selection will be, even if it will make it harder to leave players out. So there will definitely be changes but we want to win the game. We want to be competitive but we have to see how the legs are. We want to be in the next round.”

item.title: Fleetwood manager tells players not to fear Arsenal
item.description: Fleetwood manager tells players not to fear Arsenal Fleetwood Town manager Matt Lawlor has told his players to embrace the occasion rather than fear it as Arsenal arrive at Highbury Stadium in the Carabao Cup. Photo by Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor has told his players they cannot afford to be frightened of Arsenal when the Premier League champions arrive at Highbury Stadium in the Carabao Cup tonight. The League Two side have already knocked out Sheffield United to reach the fourth round and now have the chance to book a place in the quarter-finals against Mikel Arteta ’s side. Lawlor knows exactly how difficult the task is, but wants Fleetwood to enjoy the occasion rather than allow Arsenal’s status to get to them. “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch,” he said. “The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof. Photo by Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images “We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that. “To be able to represent the town on the national stage is amazing.” Lawlor has not hidden his frustration with Fleetwood’s current run of form after their good start to the season. Unbeaten in the first six, they have lost five of their last seven. “It has been a frustration of mine, and I’ve shared that with the group,” Lawlor added. “With a young group you get peaks and troughs. We need to level out a little bit more than we have done in recent weeks. It’s not from a lack of trying or effort.” This is the first time Arsenal have ever played at Highbury Stadium. item.title: Zibi Boniek says Juventus are just two nice as a team
item.description: Zibi Boniek says Juventus are just two nice as a team Zibi Boniek won five major honours with Juventus, so he knows when a team is ready to find success and when it is too nice to enjoy that, and the current Juve team does not seem ready to him. The Bianconeri have been one of the top teams in the world, but in recent times, they are not even among the best in Serie A as they simply cannot be trusted to win any game. There have been times when small teams are afraid to face the Old Lady, but nowadays, they always feel that they have a chance to win the games. Juve has been rebuilding for several seasons, yet every summer it seems like a new rebuild is starting for them all over again. Boniek’s Grim Assessment They have hired several managers, yet the team is not commanding and is nowhere near the side that dominated under Antonio Conte and Max Allegri before 2020. This Juve team is very far from being a successful side, and Boniek is understandably sad to watch them struggle, as has been the case in recent times. He has now spoken about the current Bianconeri side and believes they are just too nice. He said via Calciomercato : “It’s a pretty compromised and difficult situation. I see and hear various critics: those who are pro Conte, those who criticize Spalletti… I’m just saying that, when I look at Juventus, I don’t see a team of champions, just good players. And that makes a difference. Today they are a team not in the front row for the Scudetto, you can also see how they are suffering in Europe”. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images) A Club Searching for Identity Boniek’s words reflect a deep concern about the direction of the club, as the comparison to the Conte and Allegri eras is stark. The current side lacks the winning mentality that defined those teams, and the fans are frustrated. The rebuild has taken too long, and the club must find a way to arrest the decline. The manager’s task is to restore belief, but the scale of the challenge is significant. The coming weeks will show whether the team can respond.

item.title: MLB World Series national anthem sparks WNBA debate
item.description: Photo by Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images A routine pre-game tradition at the World Series has turned into a discussion around the WNBA. The WNBA found itself back in the crosshairs during the Finals after both Atlanta and Golden State skipped the national anthem, heading straight down the tunnel instead. Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase tried cooling the temperature, claiming it was nothing political and simply how they run their pregame. That didn’t stop the outrage machine from firing up, though. Donald Trump took straight aim at the league over the move, while also piling into LeBron James after a clip surfaced of the NBA icon casually stretching and taking imaginary golf swings while the anthem played. MLB shows the WNBA how it’s done with national anthem at World Series Before Game 3 of the MLB World Series kicked off between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field, country star Carly Pearce stepped up to belt out the national anthem. Both dugouts lined up along the chalk with caps pressed to their chests, putting on a united front. It was standard baseball tradition, but it ended up striking a chord with fans looking to make a point. Fans point to the clear disconnect between the WNBA and the MLB, with many stating that the Brewers and Rays showed how the national anthem should be done. One fan said: “HEY @WNBA watch and learn. This is game 3 of the World Series and every game, every player stands with caps on chest, showing proper respect for our national anthem. This is how it’s done. YOU SHOULD TRY IT.” “America’s sport done the American way.” Another added. This supporter added: “They could fix it, but they’d rather have controversy than quality!” “@WNBA stand for our national anthem. What is your problem?” Said one fan. Lastly, a fan pointed out how the MLB sets the standard: “MLB has its problems, but it never insults the USA.” Ditching the anthem just feels completely counterproductive. When the league spends so much time begging people to focus on the hoops and give the players their flowers, walking into an obvious culture war trap makes zero sense. Why moan that nobody’s talking about the basketball when you’re handing critics free ammo? Tottenham’s long-term contract with the 27-year-old, his strong relationship with manager Roberto De Zerbi and his current status at the club have made a potential transfer increasingly complicated. Porro has attracted attention from both Spanish giants as they assess their right-back options. Yet Tottenham’s determination to retain one of their key players could prevent either club from making progress in the short term. Pedro Porro transfer puts Real Madrid on alert Porro’s performances have made him an attractive option for Real Madrid and Barcelona, who are both monitoring the right-back market. Real Madrid are interested in Pedro Porro. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) As such, Real Madrid’s search for a reliable solution has attracted particular attention. This is because Trent Alexander-Arnold has yet to fully convince, while Denzel Dumfries is also not viewed as the ideal answer. Hence, Federico Valverde has consequently been used on the right to provide additional depth, highlighting the need for a more established option in the position. Barcelona have their own reasons to monitor Porro, but competition from Real Madrid would be problematic for both teams. What happens now? Tottenham have considerable leverage because Porro renewed his contract until 2031, with an option for an additional year. Pedro Porro is happy at Tottenham Hotspur. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) The club has also demonstrated their appreciation for the defender, giving him a guard of honour on his return following Spain’s World Cup triumph. Porro is said to be happy in London and has maintained an excellent relationship with De Zerbi. He remained supportive of the manager during a difficult start to the campaign, and Tottenham have since moved away from the relegation zone following a period of poor results. Tottenham’s negotiating position is strengthened by Porro’s contract and importance to the squad. The club is known for demanding substantial fees for their players, meaning any offer from Real Madrid would likely need to be significant before negotiations could advance.

item.description: FBL-FRA-LIGUE1-PSG-MONACO - AFP Juventus have identified USMNT international Folarin Balogun as their priority attacking target ahead of the January transfer window. The out-of-favour Monaco striker is desperate for a fresh start after a proposed deadline-day move to Everton collapsed following his medical. Juventus target USMNT star for January Juventus have reportedly made Balogun their primary attacking target for the upcoming January transfer window. The Italian side are keen to bolster their forward line heading into the second half of the campaign, according from Tuttosport . Balogun is enduring a highly frustrating spell at Monaco and looks destined to depart the club in the near future. The 25-year-old has managed a mere 71 minutes of action so far this season, pushing him towards an imminent exit. A mid-season departure now looks to be the most logical solution for all parties involved. Juventus are leading the race to secure his signature, which would finally end his challenging stint in France. Everton move collapsed after medical tests A winter transfer to Turin would follow a dramatic summer deadline day for the American attacker. Monaco had successfully agreed a permanent £40 million (€48m) deal with Everton for his services before the window slammed shut. However, Balogun ultimately rejected the move to Everton at the eleventh hour. The striker sensationally walked away from the transfer after already undergoing medical tests with the Premier League club, opting instead to remain with Monaco. Despite that hefty £40m valuation, Juventus have a significant advantage in any upcoming negotiations. The club maintains an excellent relationship with Balogun's agent, Jorge Mendes, who is reportedly eager to offer his client to Juventus. Juve seek further attacking reinforcements The pursuit of Balogun highlights a clear desire for consistent goalscoring firepower in Turin. Bianconeri are actively seeking further attacking reinforcements despite investing heavily during the recent summer transfer window. The club previously welcomed Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade to their forward ranks to share the attacking burden. item.title: Manu Kone remains in Liverpool’s sights
item.description: Manu Kone remains in Liverpool’s sights Liverpool are strongly targeting Manu Koné. The Roma midfielder, currently sidelined due to an injury, remains one of the players being monitored by the English club ahead of the upcoming winter transfer window. This interest appears to have continued despite the Frenchman’s injury, with his return expected after the November break. The Reds’ management is reportedly evaluating the possibility of strengthening the midfield as early as January, although the arrival of a new player in that area is not a top priority. According to British journalist Ben Jacobs, Koné’s name remains among those being considered by Liverpool, who are monitoring several options before deciding whether to make a move. Roma’s Frenchman isn’t the only midfielder being pursued by the English club. Bournemouth’s Scott and Monaco’s Camara are also on the list of potential targets, two alternatives that would confirm the Reds’ desire to keep several options open. At the moment, however, there are no indications of an official offer or the start of negotiations with the Giallorossi. For Roma, Manu Koné’s future could therefore once again be the focus of transfer rumors in the coming weeks: last summer, Chelsea attempted to snatch him from the Roman club in the final hours of the transfer window, but the deal was unsuccessful. The midfielder remains under observation in the Premier League, while his immediate goal is to recover from injury and return to full fitness after the league break.

(Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On the heels of their injury-riddled 19-15 victory over Indiana on Oct. 17, Ohio State had the week off to prepare for their upcoming trip to Los Angeles. The extra Saturday could not have come at a better time. With Julian Sayin out indefinitely, the Buckeyes needed the break to sort out their quarterback situation and study up on what to expect against USC. Their opponents are having an identity crisis of their own. Last Saturday night in Madison, USC looked nothing like a team that Ohio State should fear, even in a Halloween matchup. The then-No.16 Trojans managed just one touchdown against an unranked Wisconsin team, threw two first-half interceptions, and were plagued by sacks and missed field goals, falling 24-7. Whether the Buckeyes will face the version of USC that was once ranked as high as No. 12 in the nation or the one that crumbled against the Badgers last weekend remains to be seen. The Buckeyes will, thankfully, have plenty of game film to study either way. But one messy performance from the Trojans doesn’t mean Ohio State can get complacent. Last weekend doesn’t erase what USC is capable of, nor does it guarantee the Buckeyes will have an easy night in Los Angeles, especially with an inexperienced quarterback. If anything, the Buckeyes need to be prepared for a USC that’s angry, motivated, and ready to prove itself. Still, whether USC got caught looking ahead toward the game against the Buckeyes or merely just had an off-day, Wisconsin exposed several vulnerabilities that Ohio State can theoretically use to its advantage. The Trojans entered their matchup with Wisconsin averaging 36.4 points per game. Against the Badgers, however, despite outgaining their opponents on offense, the Trojans struggled to convert opportunities into points, finishing with the fewest number of points in Lincoln Riley’s tenure with the program. Wisconsin was dominant at the line of scrimmage, logging five sacks and nine tackles for loss against the Trojans, who finished the game with minus-17 net rushing yards. This bodes well for the Buckeye defense, which held the Hoosiers to just 73 rushing yards on 29 carries, an average of just 2.5 yards per carry. If Ohio State can maintain a consistent level of defensive pressure and study how Wisconsin created problems for USC, they might be able to find cracks they can exploit as well. One area where this becomes particularly important is at the line of scrimmage. Is there anything surprising about how the early season has gone for the Avalanche? Jackie: Let’s start with some positives: the third line of all new players has been a pleasant surprise. That being Jaden Schwartz, Fedor Svechkov and TJ Hughes. For years the Avs have been in search of a third line that has an identity and has enough chemistry with production to stay together, so far it’s been encouraging with each forward scoring at least twice. On the flip side, the way the Avs have degraded analytically is a surprise even with the downgrades to the roster. A 47.24% expected goals on the season, which puts Colorado at 21st in the league, is not what you’d expect from a team that’s been analytic darlings for years. Yes, 12 games is still a small sample size but coupled with the competitive and results-based inconsistencies we have seen, there are some emerging red flags. One, that even with some unkind numbers the team leads the league in shooting percentage at 14.23%, with 39 goals scored on 26 expected at 5v5. The Avs are a team that generally outscores their expected by a small margin but at nearly double means a hard regression is coming and that they are not as great at generating offense as they seem. item.title: Logan Reilly, Preston Stout topple Scottie Scheffler's East Lake Cup scoring record
item.description: Auburn sophomore Logan Reilly and Oklahoma State senior Preston Stout had a round for the record books Monday at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta. The duo, two of the best amateurs in the world, fired rounds of 7-under 65 to share medalist honors after the lone stroke-play round at the 2026 East Lake Cup. The matching 65s set a tournament scoring record, which Scottie Scheffler held for a decade following his 66 in the 2016 edition of the East Lake Cup . More: College golf's next stars? These 10 men's freshmen are worth watching in 2026-27 Reilly led for a majority of the day, but a poor drive on 18 forced him to scramble for par to share medalist honors with Stout, the world No. 1 amateur who birdied his last three holes to join Reilly on top of the leaderboard. “It was nice to feel some nerves,” Stout said. “It's always fun being under pressure. That's why we practice. I love getting in those moments and having putts like that.” Auburn earned the top seed for match play and will face Arizona while No. 2 Oklahoma State will battle UCLA come Tuesday. On the women's side, Arkansas senior Maria Jose Marin claimed medalist honors after signing for 5-under 67, besting USC junior Jasmine Koo by two shots. It's the seventh win of Marin's career. “I asked my coach where we were standing because I had no idea what was happening,” Marin said coming down the stretch. “I knew (Koo) was kind of close to me, and she said, ‘Well, if you make this putt, you might win.’ My mind gets to a point where the only thing that matters is the hole. That was what was going through my head on that last putt.” USC earned the No. 1 seed for match play on the women's side and will battle Oklahoma State while Arkansas will take on Eastern Michigan. Tuesday will feature semifinal matches for both men's and women's competition before Wednesday brings the championship final and consolation match. item.title: Red Wings Rookie Pulls Off Something Few Expected Against Oilers
item.description: VANCOUVER, CANADA - OCTOBER 22: Goalie Michal Postava #35 of the Detroit Red Wings makes a save against the Vancouver Canucks during the third period at Rogers Arena on October 22, 2026 in Vancouver, Canada. (Photo by Rich Lam/Getty Images) Getty It wasn’t that Red Wings rookie Michal Postava won in his first NHL start. It was the way he helped knock off the Edmonton Oilers. There may be nothing more frightening than recording your first NHL start against Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl, and a team that is second in the league in scoring with 51 goals (48 goals before Postava faced them). Add in the shootout so the Red Wings could skate away with two points? Few would have thought any rookie goaltender capable. Yet Postava sealed the Red Wings’ win on Monday night when he denied McDavid, Draisaitl, and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins in the shootout. Thanks to Lucas Raymond scoring in the shootout and Postava stopping three of Edmonton’s best scorers, Detroit snuck away with a big win two days after losing to a winnable opponent. What a way for Postava to kick off his NHL career after he made a cameo in the final period against the Vancouver Canucks a few days back. He didn’t look half bad against the mighty Oilers, stopping 25 of 28 shots, good for an .893 save percentage. Overall, Postava now has an .889 save percentage and a 2.89 GAA on his early-career resume. Michal Postava Turning Heads For The Detroit Red Wings This time last season, Sebastian Cossa was going to be the guy in the net for Detroit. Perhaps sidling in as a backup in Detroit for a season before taking the net as the full-time starter in 2027-28 or 2028-29. Then Postava came out of nowhere in Grand Rapids . He posted a .937 save percentage, a 1.71 GAA, and four shutouts across 25 games. He went 17-6-1 as a starter, and he followed up his regular-season success in the postseason with a 4-4 record, a .912 save percentage, a 2.09 GAA, and a shutout. After looking good in four of his appearances in Grand Rapids this season, Postava deserved and got the call-up when Daniil Tarasov went down with an injury. When Gibson had something land in his eye following the first two periods of Detroit’s win over the Canucks, Postava made his Red Wings regular-season debut. Now that he has played well against the Edmonton Oilers, the question is: what can he do against teams without facing two of arguably the best forwards in the game? Not to mention that the Oilers also have Evan Bouchard, one of the highest-scoring defensemen in hockey. Given Postava’s play in Grand Rapids and Detroit, chances are he would more than hold his own.
